label: prop:dilog-pentagon-is-associator
title: The pentagon coherence is equivalent to being a $q$-dilogarithm
html:
Fix the monoidal argument operations — the product x,y \mapsto xy, the complement x \mapsto 1-x, and division. A potential f on the shuffle algebra \mathcal{H}_q satisfies the Mac Lane pentagon (the five-term relation)

  f(y) + f(x) = f(xy) + f\!\left(\frac{x(1-y)}{1-xy}\right) + f\!\left(\frac{y(1-x)}{1-xy}\right)

if and only if it is the evaluation map of a q-dilogarithm datum with those arguments.

The equivalence holds because a q-dilogarithm datum is defined by this pentagon, so it restates that definition. It does not show that the rigid-monoidal axioms of \mathbf{C} force \mathrm{Li}_2^q; that requires the categorical-to-scalar reduction stated in the scope boundary below. Together with the uniqueness of the level-2 primitive (inhabitation of the q-dilogarithm structure), the pentagon axiom names \mathrm{Li}_2^q.

Two guises of the one pentagon

The same Mac Lane coherence has already appeared above in two guises, which this proposition records as one law:

  • Cochain / 3-cocycle guise. The additive twist associator \alpha = dF satisfies the pentagon automatically because d^2 = 0.
  • Dilogarithm five-term guise. The pentagon condition of the q-dilogarithm datum, whose operator form is the Faddeev–Kashaev pentagon \Phi(\mathsf P)\Phi(\mathsf Q) = \Phi(\mathsf Q)\Phi(\mathsf P+\mathsf Q)\Phi(\mathsf P) (the q-dilogarithm pentagon as the monoidal associator axiom).

A third, braided guise is in the literature at a root of unity. McPhail-Snyder and Reshetikhin show that the holonomy braiding of U_\xi(\mathfrak{sl}_2) at a positive, non-pinched, log-colored crossing factors as \tfrac1N Z_b(Z_r \otimes Z_l) Z_t, each factor defined by a quantum dilogarithm [mcphail-snyder-reshetikhin2025, §4.3, Thm. 4.5, eq. (4.19)], and that these R-matrices satisfy a holonomy Yang--Baxter equation for admissible colorings [mcphail-snyder-reshetikhin2025, §4.4, Thm. 4.7]. That is a statement about the braiding at a root of unity; it does not supply the scalar equivalence of this proposition or the categorical-to-scalar reduction of the scope boundary below.

Proof outline

The biconditional holds over an arbitrary carrier with an addition, with no further structure. The forward direction packages the solution of the pentagon as a q-dilogarithm datum; the reverse reads the datum's five-term condition.

Scope boundary

The equivalence is at the level of the scalar pentagon potential. The categorical \to scalar reduction (that the morphism-level Mac Lane pentagon on \alpha_{X,Y,Z} reduces to this scalar five-term equation) is the classical shuffle–associator identification of Faddeev–Kashaev; the analytic five-term relation at q \neq 1 remains conjectural.
